key_insight: A synchronization-theoretic autoencoder can map cylinder-airfoil wake interaction onto a low-dimensional oscillator model and identify conditions where vortex shedding is suppressed, i.e., oscillation death.
engineering_relevance: This offers a data-driven way to predict wake stability and interaction regimes for body-body aerodynamics, which is useful for designing bluff-body and airfoil configurations with reduced unsteady loads.
method: Direct numerical simulation of 2D incompressible flow at Reynolds number 100 for a cylinder with a NACA0012 airfoil in its wake.
Parameter sweep over streamwise gap Δx, vertical offset Δy, and airfoil angle of attack α to classify vortex-shedding regimes.
Synchronization-theoretic autoencoder built from aerodynamic coefficients to infer coupled-oscillator dynamics and stability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports four characteristic vortex-shedding regimes across the parameter space and highlights one arrangement where shedding is suppressed, with theoretical stability predicted on a machine-learned low-order coordinate.
watch_item: The results are demonstrated only for 2D Reynolds-number-100 DNS, so generalization to 3D, higher-Re flows, or different geometries may require retraining and validation.
paper_title: Studying oscillation death in two-dimensional cylinder-airfoil interactions with synchronization-theoretic autoencoder
